To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we did not find germ line mutations at the specific coding sequence of BRCA1- IRIS in any of the 116 samples from breast/ ovarian families.

we did not find any BRCA1- IRIS mutation in 116 high risk breast/ovarian cancer families, suggesting a marginal or no role of BRCA1- IRS germ-line mutations in the etiology of these tumors in our population.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of BRCA1- IRIS in breast cancer susceptibility is still uncertain and needs further investigation in larger series of high-risk families.
BRCA1- IRIS is not a breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility gene.
germ-line mutations at BRCA1- IRIS sequence are rare and probably do not play a significant role in breast cancer susceptibility in high-risk Spanish breast/ovarian cancer families.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRCA1- IRIS is a new product that is part of the BRCA 1 locus, but that it is not a major determinant of breast cancer susceptibility.
germ-line mutations at specific BRCA1 coding sequences are probably not a major determinant of high-risk breast cancer susceptibility in the Spanish population.
BRCA1-iris mutations are not associated with a significant fraction of breast/ovarian high-risk families in our population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specific BRCA-IRIS sequence is unlikely to be involved in the majority of high-risk breast and ovarian families.
it is important to screen the specific BRCA-IRIS sequence as well as the entire BRCA1 gene in high-risk breast/ ovarian families.

the screening for mutations at the specific coding sequence of BRCA1- IRIS in high-risk breast/ ovarian families should be performed only if the analysis of the whole coding sequence of BRAC1 and BRCA2 has not revealed any germ-line mutation.
